timestampOnlyOriginalRun.semantics: Original timed run bytecode retained. Additional timestamps and stderr output outside measured run; unified log timemillis granularity1ms, LogCompilation stamps rounded milliseconds. Sample8/11 planner spikes overlap two blockingC2tasks; no corresponding GC/safepoint in logs.

rerunOriginalPairedProbe.scope: Unmodified original .58 common harness compiled separately against frozen .57/.58 ownership classes. Same original32shape warmups/21samples/-Xbatch; diagnostic reproduction, not a corrected steady-state server estimate. No production code changed.

correctedWarmupControl.scope: One paired mechanism control after the execution environment reboot; separately compiled common harness, frozen .57/.58 classes. No simultaneous server/build/test. Extra warmup changes the measurement protocol, not production code. Not an independent three-round speedup claim.

conclusion: The reproduced historical two~5-7ms planner spikes are blockingC2compilation of JDK List.of/listCopy under-Xbatch after insufficient per-shape warmup. No production conflict/validator bypass or cross-tick cache was introduced. JFR itself changes the compilation threshold timeline; absence of the same spike under recording is not a fix.
limitations: Attribution applies to the reproduced specific synthetic spikes, not all real-server tails
Original21sample p95 is the second largest sample, not a long-run percentile
Warm/async/JFR controls change runtime conditions; do not report them as a production speedup
Single-thread constant predicates and sequential scopes cannot measure real worker contention or dynamic Minecraft proof cost
Other non-compilation scheduling/CPU/GC spikes are retained; no unsupported cause is assigned
